canonicalPlan.intro: I’d shape this as four deliberately light days across the park’s different gateways rather than trying to connect everything in one long push. The strongest wildlife-and-photography day is Shark Valley; the southern park road and Flamingo give you the scenic-drive component; Gulf Coast offers a quieter wildlife-watching finish. Because you haven’t set dates or a base town, the sequence below is geographic rather than tied to exact drive times—Everglades is spread out, so changing lodging bases can materially change the order. I’ve also kept walking optional and avoided treating the 15-mile Shark Valley loop as a casual hike.

narrativeSections.heading: Access and pacing
narrativeSections.markdown: Plan the south-park days together if you stay near Homestead, and pair Shark Valley with Gulf Coast only if your lodging makes that practical. US 41/Tamiami Trail currently has restoration roadwork that may add delays of up to 15 minutes, so leave slack on the Shark Valley and Gulf Coast days. Park conditions can change, and the current NPS alerts page also lists wildfire information; check it again once your dates are set. Fee stations accept only digital passes or credit/debit cards, not cash. [NPS alerts and conditions](https://www.nps.gov/ever/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)

days.label: South-park orientation and an unhurried scenic drive

stops.name: Ernest F. Coe Visitor Center
stops.note: Start with the exhibits, orientation film, and a ranger conversation about wildlife activity and same-day conditions. The center is the park gateway closest to Homestead; published hours are 8 AM–5 PM in winter and 9 AM–5 PM in summer.
stops.why: It gives you context before the long south-park drive and lets current conditions guide where you linger.

stops.name: Homestead entrance-to-Flamingo scenic drive
stops.note: Use the drive itself as the day’s main experience: keep the schedule loose, stop only at signed and legally accessible scenic areas, and spend time photographing broad wetland landscapes rather than collecting stops. Exact pullouts and access should be chosen from the park map and ranger advice that day.
stops.why: This gives scenic variety without turning the first day into a demanding activity checklist.

stops.name: Guy Bradley Visitor Center at Flamingo
stops.note: Use the displays and ranger information to focus the day around wildlife activity near Flamingo. The center is open year-round, but check same-day alerts before setting out.
stops.why: It is the best supported starting point for a slow day in the Flamingo district.

stops.name: Flamingo marina and public boat-ramp area
stops.note: Spend a flexible photography block around the developed waterfront area near the visitor center, staying out of launch traffic and following posted wildlife-distance rules. The marina store and public boat ramp are located nearby; availability of any concession activity should be checked separately.
stops.why: A patient, stationary approach suits wildlife photography better than rushing into another district.

stops.name: Flamingo developed area rest and scenic finish
stops.note: Take a long rest or picnic in the developed Flamingo area, then use the remaining light for another short waterfront look if conditions are comfortable. Do not add an unnamed trail unless rangers can verify access and suitability that day.
stops.why: It keeps this day intentionally slow and leaves room for wildlife sightings that reward waiting.

stops.name: Shark Valley Visitor Center
stops.note: Arrive in the morning for exhibits, the park film, and current guidance. Published visitor-center hours are 9 AM–5 PM.
stops.why: This is the gateway to the panoramic loop and lets you verify how to experience it without committing to a long walk.

stops.name: Shark Valley 15-mile loop and observation tower
stops.note: Make the panoramic loop the day’s anchor, preferably through the on-site tram concession if its schedule and space work for your dates. The loop is 15 miles, so it does not fit the spirit of this easygoing plan as a full walk. Confirm tram operation, booking requirements, and observation-tower access before relying on them.
stops.timeWindow: Late morning or early afternoon · reservation-dependent
stops.why: This is the plan’s best combination of broad views, wildlife watching, and photography without needing to stack extra activities.

stops.name: Shark Valley gateway photography
stops.note: Leave an unstructured block near the visitor-center gateway for patient wildlife and landscape photography from permitted developed areas. Keep clear of wildlife and obey all posted closures and instructions.
stops.why: Extra waiting time is more useful for your priorities than adding another distant stop.

days.label: Gulf Coast wildlife watching and Tamiami scenery

stops.name: Marjory Stoneman Douglas Visitor Center at Gulf Coast
stops.note: Begin with the visitor center and use its wildlife-watching setting as the day’s main slow-paced experience. The site also has a kayak launch and picnic area; published hours are 9 AM–5 PM.
stops.why: This gives the fourth day a distinct coastal character and supports wildlife viewing without requiring a hike.

stops.name: Gulf Coast kayak-launch wildlife watching
stops.note: Settle in near the developed launch area for a patient wildlife and photography session without assuming a paddle trip. Keep the launch clear and follow posted access and wildlife rules.
stops.why: It turns a simple developed area into a purposeful, low-effort photography block.

stops.name: Gulf Coast picnic area
stops.note: Take a relaxed lunch and decide whether conditions justify more wildlife watching before the drive back.
stops.why: A real pause keeps the final day from becoming another long transit-and-checklist day.

stops.name: US 41 / Tamiami Trail scenic return
stops.note: Treat the return along US 41 as the final scenic component, allowing extra time for current restoration roadwork. Stop only at signed, legal, and open areas; I could not verify specific pullouts from the information available.
stops.why: It provides a low-effort landscape finish while keeping the day geographically coherent.

I’ve kept the individual visits deliberately loose so you can linger when wildlife or light is good. narrativeSections.markdown: These areas sit at different park gateways, so treat each as its own outing rather than trying to combine them. Bring a card or digital pass for entrance payment; fee collection areas do not accept cash.

stops.name: Shark Valley Visitor Center

stops.name: Shark Valley Observation Tower and 15-mile Loop

stops.why: This is the strongest panoramic landscape experience in the plan.

stops.name: Guy Bradley Visitor Center (at Flamingo)
stops.note: Spend a little time with the displays and brochures, then use the surrounding waterfront facilities as the setting for a slow wildlife and photography outing.
stops.why: It is the Flamingo base for interpreting the area and choosing how long to linger outdoors.

stops.name: Flamingo Marina and Public Boat Ramp
stops.note: Set aside an unhurried waterfront block near the visitor center for wildlife watching and photographs. A marina store, public boat ramp, campground facilities, and nearby trails and canoeing trails are in this area.
stops.why: The waterfront setting gives this day a different visual character from Shark Valley.

stops.name: Marjory Stoneman Douglas Visitor Center (Gulf Coast)

stops.why: It places you directly at the Gulf Coast gateway and its wildlife-watching area.

stops.name: Gulf Coast Wildlife Watching and Picnic Area
stops.note: Keep the afternoon open for patient wildlife watching and photography near the visitor center, with the picnic area available for a long, unhurried break.
stops.why: A slower shoreline-oriented finish that directly suits your wildlife and photography priorities.
